subject: Re: Migration incentives and commercial terms for MerchantTech
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.k@redwood.example>
To: Alex Moreno <alex@merchanttech.io>
Cc: procurement@merchanttech.io
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Migration incentives and commercial terms for MerchantTech

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the demo last week. Based on our conversation and the usage snapshot you shared, I put together an initial migration proposal and a short-term incentive to make a move from your current provider easier. I attached the proposal (redwood-proposal-v1.pdf) and a simple cost model you can drop numbers into (merchanttech-cost-model.xlsx).

High-level summary:
- 12-month committed plan with step-down pricing by token tier
- One-time migration credit to offset data transfer and engineering effort ($40k)
- 3 months of full onboarding support (priority queue + 2 on-site/virtual sprints)
- SLA: 99.9% availability, with credit schedule outlined in the appendix

Before I lock down numbers with finance, two asks:
1) Can you confirm the current committed term and effective per-token rate your incumbent is offering?
2) Any blockers on data residency / KMS that we should bake into the commercial terms?

If it helps, I can put together a short mutual action plan (MAP) and a DocuSign-ready term sheet once we confirm the target economics.

If youre free Monday/Tuesday Ill hold a slot for a 30-min follow-up to walk the numbers.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vivek.k@redwood.example | +1 415-555-0123

Attachment: redwood-proposal-v1.pdf, merchanttech-cost-model.xlsx

From: Alex Moreno <alex@merchanttech.io>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.k@redwood.example>
Cc: procurement@merchanttech.io
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 10:43:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Migration incentives and commercial terms for MerchantTech

Vivek —

Thanks for the fast follow. Were evaluating two options now (you and CloudPrompt). A few clarifications on our side:

1) Incumbent economics: CloudPrompt is offering us an effective blended rate of $0.00055 per token on a 12-month commit (~$720k ARR equivalent) plus a $50k migration credit and a one-time credit against professional services. Theyre also proposing a pilot 90-day escape clause with 30-day notice.

2) Residency/KMS: We need EU data residency for EU customers and a bring-your-own-key (BYOK) option for sensitive logs. Thats non-negotiable for a subset of traffic.

3) Packaging ask: Can Redwood match the $50k migration credit and provide a similar pilot concession? Also curious if you can offer a short-term accelerated on-ramp price for high-variance Q1 volume spikes — our forecast is noisy.

If you can circulate an updated term sheet showing a matching migration credit and clarity on residency/KMS within the week, procurement will prioritize reviewing it.

Thanks —
Alex Moreno
Head of Platform Engineering | MerchantTech
alex@merchanttech.io

(On Mon, Feb 22, 2027 at 09:18 AM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.k@redwood.example> wrote:

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.k@redwood.example>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.example>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.example>
Date: Tue, 23 Feb 2027 08:07:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Migration incentives and commercial terms for MerchantTech

Ben / Marissa —

Forwarding MerchantTechs counter. They want a $50k migration credit and a 90-day pilot escape similar to CloudPrompt. Also strict EU residency + BYOK for some traffic.

Quick asks:
- Ben: can we structure a deal that preserves unit economics if we match the $50k credit? Thinking: 12-month commit with minimum volume floors + 3-tier overage pricing; apply the credit over first 3 invoices rather than one lump sum. Any concerns on margin if we add an accelerated Q1 spike protection?
- Marissa: procurement asked about a 30-day pilot termination clause — do we accept a 90-day pilot with 30-day notice or need different language? Also need input on data-residency/KMS contractual language.

Ive penciled an alternative:
- $50k migration credit amortized over first three months (reduces cash exposure)
- 12-mo commit at slightly higher token rates but with step-down at +25% volumetric thresholds
- Pilot: 90 days, but with limited production SLA exposure during pilot (no financial credits)
- EU residency + BYOK: treat as SOW/implementation scope with escrowed timelines and milestone-based acceptance

Can you both review and advise by EOD tomorrow? MerchantTech expects an updated term sheet this week.

Thanks —
Vivek

--
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.k@redwood.example>

Cc: procurement@redwood.tech; ben.carter@redwood.example; marissa.cole@redwood.example
Date: Thu, 25 Feb 2027 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Migration incentives and commercial terms for MerchantTech

Alex —

Appreciate the clarity and the competitor details. We reviewed internally and can meet MerchantTechs needs with the following updated commercial offer (attached: redwood-offer-v2.pdf):

Summary of revised offer:
- Commit: 12 months, $650k ARR-equivalent (volume tiers inside the sheet)
- Migration credit: $50,000, amortized across the first three invoices (applies to professional services & onboarding)
- Pilot: 90-day pilot with a 30-day notice escape; pilot operates under a limited SLA (operational support, no financial SLA credits until GA)
- Data residency/BYOK: We will enable EU-region tenancy and support BYOK for keys via our KMS integration; residency is scoped in the SOW with milestoneed delivery (estimated 6-8 weeks for initial EU tenancy)
- Onboarding: 3 full sprints of onboarding + one week of dedicated support during ramp (priority response)
- Addendum: We include an option for a one-time accelerated capacity burst protection for Q1 at a pre-agreed uplift so you dont face sudden overage pricing for forecast variance (details in the offer)

Next steps I propose:
1) Well push a DocuSign-ready term sheet to the link below with the updated numbers and a standard data residency addendum.
2) If procurement signals green, we can schedule an internal kickoff and pick target dates for the EU tenancy workstream.

DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/MT-Migration-Offer
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345

Attachments: redwood-offer-v2.pdf (term sheet + MAP)

Can you confirm today whether the amortized credit approach and the pilot language is acceptable? If yes Ill start the DocuSign flow and loop Legal for the residency addendum.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Vivek —

Thanks for the quick turn. MerchantTech is comfortable in principle with the commercial structure you outlined. A couple of final asks before procurement will sign:

1) Can we include a short clause in the data residency addendum that mandates EU-only processing for EU-customer traffic, with a 30-day remediation SLA if misrouting is detected?
2) For the pilot escape, can we add a 30-day termination window on either side during the pilot (so both parties can exit with notice)?

If youve got DocuSign ready with that language and the amortized $50k credit spelled out, procurement will sign and well aim to start onboarding the week of March 15.

Ill have procurement confirm formally once they see the redline.

Appreciate the partnership — looking forward to getting this over the line.
